author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
description:
Carney watches on as comedian lampoons US leader and his interest in men’s backsides at correspondents’ event Ottawa

Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, was joined on stage in Ottawa by a Donald Trump impersonator who mocked the US president to raucous laughter from a crowd of politicians and journalists at a parliamentary press gallery dinner on Saturday.

With coiffed hair and an ill-fitting suit, comedian Mark Critch – who portrays the president on the sketch show This Hour Has 22 Minutes – danced on to the stage and lampooned the trade war Trump started as well as the president’s threats to annex Canada.

Continue reading...
title: Butt of the joke: Trump impersonator mocks president at Canada press dinner

author: Cecilia Nowell
description:
Democrat, who lost re-election bid, found to have made ‘unwelcome sexual advances’ towards House staffer

Jimmy Gomez will resign from Congress after a House ethics report released on Monday found “substantial evidence” that the California Democrat had “engaged in sexual misconduct”, including by “making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a House staffer”.

The 19-page report from the House ethics committee found that Gomez “made unwanted sexual advances” toward a House staffer on two occasions, “including an incident in which he made sexual contact with her and another in which he was ‘forceful’ with her in his congressional office”.

Continue reading...
title: Jimmy Gomez to resign after House ethics panel finds evidence of sexual misconduct

In June, prime minister, Anthony Albanese, and his Vanuatu counterpart, Jotham Napat, signed the Nakamal agreement in Canberra that rules out the use of its territory for foreign military bases.

We acknowledge the legitimate concerns Vanuatu and other Pacific Island nations have regarding climate change and its impacts on their communities, economies, and national security.

However, Coalition members object to clauses … that limit the ability of future governments t
title: Australian politics live: Penny Wong to defend US alliance; Coalition condemns Vanuatu deal

description:
Andy Burnham has set out his plans to win parliamentary backing for a new EU deal. But the various options for how Britain could rejoin the EU, or ‘Breturn’, will not be outlined until December. Pippa Crerar has been speaking to the prime minister about how he hopes to convince the public that reversing Brexit is worth the headache

You can tell us what you think of Guardian podcasts with our survey here

Send any questions for Pippa and Kiran to politicsweeklyuk@theguardian.com

You can watch this episode of Politics Weekly on our YouTube channel here.

author: Sandra Laville
description:
Environmentalists say abolishing independent body will make it easier for landowners and developers ‘to trash nature’

Not just any quango, Natural England is the only public body that exists to legally protect the jewels in the crown of English nature – places increasingly under threat in a country that is overseeing an ongoing and devastating decline in its natural world.

Ecologists who work for Natural England are independent, and have the legal duty to scrutinise political decisions and ensure that short-term gallops for growth are not allowed to bulldoze forever rare and declining habitats.

Continue reading...
title: Abolishing Natural England would be travesty, say campaigners

author: Anna Betts in New York
description:
City reaches deal with Lyft, parent company of Citi Bike, in effort to ‘make biking affordable for every New Yorker’

Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, announced on Monday that the city has reached an agreement with Lyft, the parent company of Citi Bike, the city’s bike-share system, to cap ebike fares for members at $3.65 for rides of up to 45 minutes, starting in mid-January.

In a video announcing the changes, the mayor’s office said that a 45-minute ebike ride currently costs members $12.15, but that under the new agreement, that price will fall to $3.65 from 19 January 2027.

Continue reading...
title: Mamdani says New York will cap ebike fares to ‘significantly’ cut cost of rides

author: Presented by Lucy Houghwith Graham Readfearn; produced by Angus Neale; senior producer Leonore Schick; executive producer Zoe Hitch
description:
Countries at the Cop31 climate summit failed to reach a keystone agreement for the first time in 17 years. The talks, co-chaired by Turkey and Australia, were intended to produce a pact that would have injected urgency into climate action and financing for vulnerable states. Instead, the deal failed after a standoff over fossil fuels and support for countries exposed to the climate crisis. Guardian Australia’s climate and environment reporter Graham Readfearn tells Lucy Hough why there are calls for urgent reform of the Cop process – watch on YouTube

Continue reading...
title: Cop31 collapses: why did climate talks fall apart? - The Latest

author: Ariana Baio
description:
DNC unveils plans to hold 12 primary debates over 10 months, allowing up to 20 candidates to participate

The Democratic National Committee (DNC) unveiled on Monday its plans to hold a dozen 2028 presidential primary debates over 10 months, with the first set to take place in June.

Between June 2027 and March 2028, the DNC will host 12 debates, allowing up to 20 candidates to participate, so long as they agree to new criteria. That includes pledging to reject “dark money” – or funding from outside groups that do not disclose their donors – and not participating in unsanctioned debates.

Continue reading...
title: Democrats to hold a dozen 2028 presidential primary debates starting in June

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Deltona officials say parade is getting cancelled due to the state’s voter-approved Amendment 3 property tax overhaul

A city in southwestern Florida has cancelled its Christmas parade, citing pending state legislation, to ensure the city remains “fiscally responsible”.

City officials in Deltona said the parade – which typically include floats, marching bands, dancers and Santa Claus appearing in the finale – was getting cancelled due to Florida’s voter-approved property tax overhaul.

Continue reading...
title: Florida city cancels Christmas parade after tax amendment forces budget cuts

description:

  • Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang – latest updates

  • US politics – live updates

Donald Trump said on Monday that he spoke “directly and indirectly” with Nvidia’s board and “convinced them” to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive.

“I’ve been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it,” Trump said on
title: Trump says he ‘convinced’ Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang

author: Ben Tracy of Climate Central
description:
Scientists are racing to identify and breed new berry varieties that can thrive on an increasingly warmer planet

It is harvest time in rural Wisconsin, and the Badger state’s most vibrant crop is painting the rolling countryside a brilliant, unmistakable red.

For nearly three decades, Nicole Hansen has been farming cranberries here. Wisconsin produces more than 60% of the nation’s supply. On a crisp fall morning, we waded into a marsh with her to round up the floating harvest.

Climate Central is an independent group of scientists and communicators that researches and reports the facts about our changing climate and how it affects people’s lives

Continue reading...
title: Cranberry jam: warming winters and extreme weather threaten an iconic holiday fruit

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Five passengers were reported to have non-life-threatening injuries after crash at railroad crossing near Lafayette

An Amtrak train collided with a tractor-trailer at a railroad crossing in south-central Louisiana, derailing the lead locomotive and two baggage cars while injuring some passengers on Sunday evening, officials said.

Five passengers who were reported hurt were said to have injuries that were not life-threatening.

Continue reading...
title: Amtrak train derails after colliding with tractor-trailer in Louisiana

author: Petra Stock
description:
Nationwide change in lunch habits could cut more climate pollution than grounding every domestic flight

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australians could collectively cut climate pollution by more than 15m tonnes – more than grounding every domestic flight – simply by changing what they eat for lunch.

A nationwide shift to plant-based lunches could reduce food-related emissions by 29% – 15.4m tonnes per year – while saving the average household about $611 annually, according to a report by Bryant Research and not-for-profit ProVeg.

Continue reading...
title: Plant-based lunches could cut Australia’s emissions by 15m tonnes, new research shows

description:
Exclusive: Alarming report reveals how tracking and monitoring functions and digital key access have been used to facilitate abuse

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Earlier this year a man in Australia was found guilty of using a connected car app to harass his former partner, including restricting the speed at which she could drive, sometimes to 40km an hour.

In 2022 in the US, a woman found her former husband had used a car app associated with her car to track her; the carmaker then allegedly refused to terminate the former partner’s digital acc
title: Domestic violence perpetrators are misusing smart car features to abuse, researchers warn

author: Edward Helmore and agencies
description:
Members of the free-expression literary and human rights group are forming a new chapter called PEN Writes US

More than 100 well-known writers and members of the literary world are to form a splinter chapter of PEN America, the free-expression literary and human rights group, over tensions within the organization over Israel’s war in Gaza and other issues.

Writers including Ta-Nehisi Coates, M Gessen and Jacqueline Woodson are among those who on Monday announced they are forming a new group called PEN Writes US that will be “guided by the PEN Charter’s vision of ‘one humanity, living in peace and equality in one world’”.

Continue reading...
title: Over 100 writers from PEN America to form splinter group over Gaza tensions

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
Australian dictionary’s committee of word experts says winning term is ‘a succinct reflection of the state of the world in 2026’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The backlash to “pervert glasses” has been swift and severe.

Smartglasses such as Meta’s Ray-Bans, which have built-in cameras, microphones, and AI assistants have been banned at some Australian swimming pools and playgrounds, and condemned as a possible invasion of privacy.
title: ‘Pervert glasses’ named word of the year by Macquarie dictionary, ahead of ‘nudify’ and ‘AI;DR’

author: Associated Press
description:
Authorities say they believe the Saturday night shooting at a concert in Strathmore ‘may be gang-related’

Nine people were shot at a concert in central California, leaving one person critically injured with a chest injury, the local sheriff said Sunday.

The shooting broke out at about 7.30pm Saturday at a concert attended by about 150 people in Strathmore, a small town in Tulare county, a mountainous region in the center of the state, the local sheriff’s department said in a statement. An unspecified number of suspects opened fire on the crowd. No arrests were announced.

Continue reading...
title: Nine people shot at central California concert with one in critical condition

author: Martin Belam
description:
More than two weeks of talks in Turkey fail to produce a resolution to tackle climate crisis. Plus, a savage review of Melania’s new documentary

Good morning. The world’s nations have failed to reach agreement at the Cop31 talks in Turkey. In a dramatic conclusion to the summit, major powers rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels. The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien.

What was in the proposed agreement? The Antalya pact invited nations to electrify their economies, called on wealthy countries to fund climate adaptation for poorer ones, and urged signatories to minimise any “overshoot” of the Paris agreement’s 1.5C global heating threshold. However, it failed to endorse the “transi
title: First Thing: Cop31 talks collapse without deal in blow to planet’s future climate

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Brian Morales García of Texas seeks damages after he was wrongly identified as undocumented in case White House wants dropped

The Trump administration recently admitted in federal court that it deported a US citizen to Mexico after American authorities incorrectly concluded he was an undocumented immigrant.

Attorneys for the US justice department made that admission on Friday while requesting the dismissal of a lawsuit for damages that the deported man – Brian José Morales García of Austin, Texas – has been pursuing against the federal government.

Continue reading...
title: Trump administration deported US citizen to Mexico, DoJ admits in court

author: Catie McLeod Consumer affairs reporter
description:
Jetstar accused of issuing customers credits instead of cash refunds for flights cancelled between 2020 and late 2022

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

More than 1 million Jetstar customers could be eligible to join a class action alleging the airline failed to refund them for flights it cancelled during the pandemic, the firm leading the lawsuit has said.

The federal court on Monday confirmed it had ordered notices be sent to customers informing them of their eligibility to participate in, or opt out of, the lawsuit, with a potential trial set for March 2027.
title: Up to 1.1m people eligible to join class action against Jetstar over alleged failure to refund Covid flights

author: Josh Butler
description:
Anne Twomey says lack of proper debate around bill is ‘flabbergasting’ amid concerns over extension of ministerial powers

Labor’s new defence bill is “lazy and irresponsible” lawmaking, one of Australia’s leading constitutional scholars has warned, claiming provisions for the government to secretly class any facility as a special security zone could raise serious legal issues.

Prime minister Anthony Albanese claimed on Monday that critics of the ‘accelerating capability and protecting bases’ bill were “jump[ing] at shadows”, accusing them of “absurd” claims. But parliamentary crossbenchers opposed to the bill, which was rushed through parliament with little public scrutiny, were joined on Monday by Prof Anne Twomey, who expressed alarm about what she called an increasing trend of ministers exercisi
title: Constitutional law expert brands defence bill allowing secret security rules ‘lazy and irresponsible’

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Gate fee comes on top of annual cost of between $300 and $700 per family

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Football clubs representing hundreds of thousands of players are preparing to break away from Football Queensland this week, saying the state governing body charges unreasonably high fees and is unaccountable.

Some parents and siblings are charged a $5 gate fee to watch children’s matches in parts of regional Queensland.

Continue reading...
title: Clubs and families revolt as Football Queensland charges $5 a head to watch children play

author: Hettie O'Brien
description:
In today’s newsletter: The prime minister has reopened the debate over a future relationship with a changed EU – as the bloc faces the rise of the far right, a protectionist economic agenda and growing defence ambitions

Good morning. Nobody really wants to think about Brexit any more, save for the original Brexiters, who seem delighted that Andy Burnham’s “reset” with the EU has given them an excuse to get the old gang back together. But arguments about whether the UK should rejoin the EU will reignite in parliament this week, as Burnham briefs MPs on the deal he agreed on Friday.

That deal wasn’t so much a victory as the culmination of Keir Starmer’s incrementalist approach to UK-EU relations. Its core agreements haven’t been ratified by member states yet, and the EU won’t sign them off until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students. Burnham is apparently “determined” to take the UK back into the EU, but don’t expect any progress on that befor
title: Monday briefing: What could Andy Burnham’s reset mean for the UK?

author: Graham Readfearn in Antalya and Josh Butler in Canberra
description:
Coalition calls for climate change minister to resign immediately or be sacked over ‘catastrophic diplomatic disaster’, despite offering no alternatives on reducing emissions

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Anthony Albanese has defended Chris Bowen from criticism following the failure of the UN Cop31 climate summit, blaming the result on “difficult geopolitical times” as the Coalition called for the minister to resign.

Bowen served as president of negotiations at the talks in Turkey, helping run the conference with his Turkish counterpart, Murat Kurum.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Difficult geopolitical times’: Albanese defends Bowen after Cop31 deal failure

Jim Chalmers has warned Australians that “things will get a bit harder before they get easier”, revealing next month’s budget update will show unemployment climbing above 5% alongside slower economic growth for the next two years.

As economists flagged rising recessionary risks, the treasurer used a ministeri
title: Unemployment to surpass 5% and ‘things will get a bit harder’, treasurer Jim Chalmers warns

Inquest into the deaths of four babies after free and home births hears doula urged client to attend birth centre

A doula who supported a free birth without any medical professionals present has told an inquest that she thought a self-described birth keeper who was assisting her was clinically trained.

The child, known in court as Baby R, died after the free birth. Baby R’s death is one of four being examined in a joint c

author: Coral Murphy Marcos
description:
Footage of Saturday incident, filmed by fellow passengers, quickly went viral on social media as mayor calls tactics ‘un-American’

Protesters marched through the Seattle-Tacoma international airport on Sunday after widely shared footage captured masked immigration agents detaining a father and daughter on an airport jet bridge as they boarded their Alaska Airlines flight.

Video of the incident on Saturday – filmed by fellow passengers – quickly went viral on social media, sparking condemnation from lawmakers, including Washington Democratic governor Bob Ferguson and Seattle mayor Katie Wilson.

Continue reading...
title: Video of ICE detaining father and daughter while boarding flight sparks protests in Seattle

description:
Crown urges jury to reject accused’s claim of self-defence and find him guilty of murdering Sydney couple

Beau Lamarre-Condon is a “proven and persistent liar” and the evidence in his double murder trial shows the deaths of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies could only have been an “execution”, a court has been told.

Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting the Sydney couple with his police service weapon in Baird’s Padding
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon ‘executed’ Jesse Baird and Luke Davies then lied about it, prosecution argues
